nodes.label: Clip Description (neutral, observational)
nodes.rationale: A Clip Description is a neutral read of one Clip (subject/action, setting/mood, usability rating), not second-person coaching. Coaching is un-actionable because the tool edits already-shot footage, and a description is the better Story signal for the Author step to sequence from. Keeps the product a neutral curator rather than a vlog-delivery critic.

nodes.label: describeClip prompt
nodes.rationale: Had drifted into a 'vlog coach' prompt; must be rewritten to describe subject/action, setting/mood and usability. Until that lands the code and the glossary disagree, and the glossary is canonical.

nodes.label: vlogMove / energy fields
nodes.rationale: Artifacts of the coaching drift on the description type; to be renamed as part of realigning code to the model.

nodes.label: Neutral curator product stance
nodes.rationale: The product discovers a Story across arbitrary footage; it does not critique vlog delivery.

nodes.label: Export text rendered by browser canvas to PNG, not ffmpeg drawtext
nodes.rationale: Preview used the browser text engine while export used ffmpeg drawtext; the gap is structural, not tunable (no CSS letter-spacing, different kerning/shaping, no wrapping so wrap was guessed at ~0.5*fontsize). No amount of tuning closes an engine mismatch, so both sides must render with the same engine. Rejected: keep tuning drawtext (cannot reach parity); SVG->PNG export with CSS preview ('both browser' is not 'same engine'); full WebCodecs/Mediabunny hybrid (deferred, its value is speed not parity).

nodes.label: Shared canvas-2D text renderer (fillText + letterSpacing + measureText wrap)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth called by both preview and export, so parity is by construction rather than approximation.

nodes.label: ffmpeg drawtext (removed from export path)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: this @ffmpeg/core build has no CSS letter-spacing (tracking crashes with 'Option not found'), kerns/shapes differently from the browser, and cannot wrap.

nodes.label: Export-pixel coordinate space
nodes.rationale: The renderer always draws at full export resolution (e.g. 1920x1080) and the preview CSS-scales that same bitmap, so both sides share one unit system and a wrap boundary can never flip between them.

nodes.label: Static bitmap, motion on top
nodes.rationale: Glyphs are baked once into a static PNG identical on both sides; the preview animates it with CSS transform/opacity while the export matches with ffmpeg overlay x/y/alpha expressions using the same linear easing. Caption cue windows are gated with overlay:enable='between(t,a,b)'.

nodes.label: Arc titles via SVG textPath
nodes.rationale: Curved text (arcDeg != 0) reuses the existing SVG textPath -> drawImage inside the one renderer, keeping arc a single source of truth without new glyph-on-path math.

nodes.label: FontFace + document.fonts.ready hard requirement
nodes.rationale: If the canvas draws before the font resolves it silently falls back to a system font and measureText wraps against the wrong metrics, so parity is lost invisibly.

nodes.label: wrapCaption glyph-width heuristic (removed)
nodes.rationale: Approximated wrapping with a ~0.5*fontsize glyph-width guess that disagreed with browser wrapping; goes away with drawtext.

nodes.label: HYBRID_EXPORT_PLAN.md (WebCodecs/Mediabunny hybrid)
nodes.rationale: Deferred as a later performance pass: a large rewrite whose value is speed, while parity does not require it.

nodes.label: Remotion (evaluated and rejected)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated July 2026 and rejected. Only the client-side renderer is compatible with ADR-0002 (no backend). mix-blend-mode is unsupported yet Overlays depend on it; the parity argument inverts because renderMediaOnWeb emulates layout onto a canvas in an experimental alpha dependency; ffmpeg.wasm would not actually leave, giving three engines instead of two; the speed win comes from WebCodecs+Mediabunny which HYBRID_EXPORT_PLAN.md targets directly; further subset gaps (no z-index, backdrop-filter, 3D transforms, OffthreadVideo, CSS filters unsupported in Safari/WebKit). Full adoption would displace ~4,280 lines. Reopened by renderMediaOnWeb gaining mix-blend-mode and leaving alpha, or by wanting React-authored motion graphics.

nodes.label: @remotion/web-renderer renderMediaOnWeb()
nodes.rationale: The only Remotion variant compatible with a no-backend constraint; encodes via WebCodecs + Mediabunny in the browser but emulates layout and supports only a subset of HTML/CSS.

nodes.label: mix-blend-mode Overlay blending
nodes.rationale: StagePreview/FinalPreview set mixBlendMode from an Overlay's blend mode and export.ts mirrors it with the ffmpeg blend filter; screen and multiply are shipped creative features, so losing them is a regression.

nodes.label: WebCodecs
nodes.rationale: The actual source of the export speed win, reachable without the Remotion intermediary and feature-detected with a clean ffmpeg.wasm fallback.

nodes.label: ADR-0002 no-backend constraint
nodes.rationale: Forecloses Remotion's server-side and Lambda renderers, which require Node and headless Chrome; also drives 1080p ingest normalisation.

nodes.label: One grade generator drives preview and export
nodes.rationale: Color had ADR-0008's two-engine problem: preview used CSS filters (multiplicative brightness, sRGB) while export used ffmpeg eq/hue/colorbalance (additive offset, YUV), and split-tone had no preview at all so the most expressive axis was graded blind. A single TS module now owns the math as one channel-mixing step composed with one per-channel curve step. Rejected: reconciling the math in place (tuning cannot close an engine mismatch and CSS still cannot tone-target); shrinking the model to what CSS expresses (loses the film look's range and still needs the reconciliation); a WebGL preview pass (unnecessary); deferring to the WebCodecs migration (blocks a visibly-wrong shipped feature behind a large unstarted project).

nodes.label: A Look is a target, not an offset
nodes.rationale: Clips shot at different exposures and white balances need different corrections to land in the same place, so Beats are graded individually toward a Look and applying it clears the global fine-tune (Undo restores both). Previously deriving a Look set the global and applying it wrote per-shot grades too, so the two summed. One deliberate exception: saving a Look as a preset still activates it globally, accepted knowingly.

nodes.label: SVG filter preview (feColorMatrix + feComponentTransfer)
nodes.rationale: Applies the generator's transform natively on the CSS filter already on the <video>, extending the inline-SVG data-URI approach; makes split-tone visible before export for the first time.

nodes.label: 3D LUT (.cube) baked for ffmpeg lut3d
nodes.rationale: The export bakes the identical composition into a .cube consumed by lut3d, replacing eq/hue/colorbalance outright; lut3d and haldclut are compiled into the self-hosted core while curves is not, so a 1D-curve export filter was not an option. Grid resolution becomes a real parameter: too coarse bands, too fine bloats the file.

nodes.label: Split-tone axes
nodes.rationale: Added so cinematic looks would be representable, but CSS cannot tone-target so it was folded into global white balance at 0.4x as an admitted 'directional hint' while the export applied real per-tonal-range colorbalance.

nodes.label: gradeBeatToLook (per-shot matched grade)
nodes.rationale: Instructs Claude to account for where the shot already sits and not double up; the composition rule doubled up anyway until the Look-as-target decision.

nodes.label: Composed grade clamped to +/-100
nodes.rationale: The range the sliders, the domain model and the AI prompt are all defined in, and the bounded input the LUT bake requires.

nodes.label: Sticker (placement on cut.stickers)
nodes.rationale: Stickers reuse two systems the project already has rather than inventing a third: the library/track half copies SFX and the rendering half obeys ADR-0008. Shaped like SfxSegment and OverlayClip (id, filename, absolute startTimeSec, durationSec) plus four spatial fields (x, y as frame fractions, scale as a fraction of frame width, rotation in degrees) and opacity. Fractions rather than pixels keep placement correct across 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1.

nodes.label: stickerCanvas.ts shared renderer
nodes.rationale: Mirrors titleCanvas.ts, composing the asset onto a full-frame transparent bitmap at export resolution so preview and export share one bitmap. Doing it any other way (CSS transform on an vs an ffmpeg overlay offset) is the exact engine mismatch ADR-0008 was written about, and rotation+scale about a centre point is where they drift; a per-Beat rotation already shipped with an inverted sign because the two sides were computed separately.

nodes.label: stickerLibrary.ts / /api/stickers dev-server plugin
nodes.rationale: Mirrors audioLibrary/sfxLibrary call for call: basename() before joining so a request cannot escape the folder, an extension allowlist, and upload writing into the same folder so an uploaded asset joins the library.

nodes.label: Sticker rotation is +/-180 degrees
nodes.rationale: A Beat's +/-15 degree rotation straightens footage where anything past a few degrees is a mistake; a Sticker's rotation is placement where any angle is legitimate. Different concepts wearing the same word.

nodes.label: Sticker favourites in localStorage
nodes.rationale: Filenames in localStorage mirroring voPresets.ts, sorted to the top of the picker like custom ElevenLabs voices. Global rather than per-Project because a Sticker the author reaches for often is a property of the author, not of one edit.

nodes.label: SVG stickers rasterised at export resolution
nodes.rationale: Drawn through an at export resolution so a large scale stays sharp - the one place a Sticker beats a pre-rendered PNG.

nodes.label: A still image is a Clip with a synthetic duration
nodes.rationale: JPG/PNG/WebP stills import through the same door as footage and become ordinary Clips; only the length is missing, so ingest invents one. durationSec: 0 would propagate as a bug rather than a signal (computeWindow clamps with Math.min, preBeats clamps footageLen, the trimmer divides by dur), and each guard is a place a future change can forget the still case. One field, kind, and one constant carry the whole feature.

nodes.label: STILL_CLIP_DURATION_SEC (10s)
nodes.rationale: The invented length, which is also the accepted ceiling: a still Beat can be trimmed shorter but not stretched longer because the trimmer bounds itself by the source. Raising the ceiling is a one-constant change; unbounded is a different feature and not v1.

nodes.label: Clip.kind (optional; undefined means video)
nodes.rationale: Optional so every project saved before the ADR loads unchanged. Read in exactly five places: ingest, beat window, the three preview surfaces, export, and the two vision paths.

nodes.label: probeStill ingest path
nodes.rationale: Uses instead of probeVideo's

nodes.label: computeWindow beat window for stills
nodes.rationale: Gives a still the whole source window [0,10] rather than a script-derived slice: ADR-0004 paces a Beat by its Script line because footage has a most-interesting moment to land on, but a still has one frame so pacing by word count buys nothing and a predictable length is worth more.

nodes.label: Still export via -loop 1 input stage
nodes.rationale: -loop 1 -t {len} -r 30 -i in.jpg replaces -ss/-t/-i in.mp4 and audio always comes from anullsrc; the same treatment captions, Title overlays and Stickers already get, and the filtergraph downstream is byte-for-byte what a video Beat builds.

nodes.label: sourceName() must consult kind before normalized
nodes.rationale: On project import projectPackager sets normalized to the original blob for every clip, so a still would otherwise be handed to ffmpeg as in.mp4; the packager now leaves a still's normalized unset.

nodes.label: One Colour field, one global palette
nodes.rationale: Before this, TitleTreatmentEditor had a hardcoded TITLE_SWATCHES of three and the Sticker tint row a different inline list of seven, so a custom colour was used once and lost and the two lists had already drifted. The palette lives in localStorage like sticker favourites, VO presets and filter presets: a colour the author reaches for is a property of the author, not of one edit. Accepted cost: the palette does not travel in a .vidstr, so a collaborator sees their own.

nodes.label: ColorField component
nodes.rationale: Presentational, takes value/onChange and does not know what it is colouring, so the next thing that needs a colour gets the palette for free. Collapses three render sites: per-beat Titles (Inspector), cut-level Titles (Export) and the Sticker tint row.

nodes.label: loadPalette() / DEFAULT_PALETTE / MAX_PALETTE
nodes.rationale: Seeds from DEFAULT_PALETTE on first read and thereafter returns exactly what is stored, so defaults are not a separate immutable tier and removal works uniformly. New colours append rather than sorting to the front because a reordering palette moves swatches out from under the cursor; a rolling MAX_PALETTE of 20 drops from the front on overflow.

nodes.label: EyeDropper API sampling
nodes.rationale: Samples a colour from anywhere on screen including the Cut preview - the point being to tint a Sticker with a colour taken out of the footage. Chromium-only, so the button is feature-detected and simply absent elsewhere; <input type="color"> remains. Anything picked through either route is added, since a colour worth sampling is a colour worth reusing.

nodes.label: usePalette() subscription
nodes.rationale: Keeps every mounted ColorField in step so adding a colour in the Sticker row updates the Title row without a remount.

nodes.label: google: font id encoded in fontId
nodes.rationale: fontId is already an opaque string that round-trips through .vidstr packages, title presets, the copy/paste style clipboard and per-beat title layers. A sibling googleFamily field would have to be added to each path and every layer literal, and any one missed is a font that silently reverts on reload. Encoding in the id means no schema change and no migration: code predating the feature only ever passed the string along.

nodes.label: findFontById(id)
nodes.rationale: One of the two seams font resolution funnels through; a google: id yields a synthetic GoogleFontOption whose cssFamily is 'Anton', sans-serif.

nodes.label: getTitleFontBytes(id, weight, file)
nodes.rationale: The second seam: returns TTF bytes for the canvas renderer and ffmpeg, building the same synthetic option for a google: id. Everything downstream (titleCanvas, export.ts, FinalPreview) is untouched because it consumes only family and bytes.

nodes.label: fetchGoogleFontBytes / Fontsource CDN
nodes.rationale: Already fetches uncompressed TTF from cdn.jsdelivr.net/fontsource/fonts/{slug}@latest/latin-{weight}-normal.ttf, exactly the format ffmpeg wants, so 'fetch and convert' is only a fetch. Falls back from the requested weight to 400, and ends in a guaranteed fallback to title-sans.ttf.

nodes.label: Picker probes the CDN so typos fail loudly
nodes.rationale: Because fetchGoogleFontBytes ends in a guaranteed fallback, a misspelled family cannot be detected from its result and would render in the wrong font. The picker probes before accepting a name and reports 'not found' instead of storing an id that quietly renders as something else.

nodes.label: Ken Burns - a Still's moving framing
nodes.rationale: A move is its own concept rather than an end state on Zoom: a Zoom is a framing decision (what is in shot) and a Ken Burns is a motion decision (what the eye does over time); collapsing them degrades Ken Burns into a checkbox on a zoom slider. Stills only for v1 because ingest normalises video to 1080p (ADR-0002) but deliberately not Stills (ADR-0012), so a push into a Still has real pixels behind it while the same push into video is upscaling - and on a Still the move is the difference between a video and a slideshow. Narrowing later is the hard direction.

nodes.label: Ken Burns and Zoom are a mutually exclusive mode
nodes.rationale: Both command the scale and centre of the frame, so composing them makes the real starting scale zoom x kenBurnsStart and every number in the UI lies. Letting the move silently win was rejected on the rule that a visible, live-looking control must not be inert (the same reason the Title layer checkbox was changed), so choosing one turns the other off.

nodes.label: ffmpeg zoompan emitter
nodes.rationale: The existing zoomChain emits scale,crop; crop's x/y animate under eval=frame giving a pan, but zooming needs the crop size to change per frame and scale does not reliably take per-frame output dimensions, so pan-and-zoom that way is a dead end. zoompan is compiled into both self-hosted wasm cores, and runs before the pad that letterboxes - after it the move would scale and slide the black bars.

nodes.label: One-time canvas pre-scale (renderStillContained)
nodes.rationale: zoompan truncates x/y to whole pixels so slow pans step visibly; the mitigation is more pixels than the output needs, bounded so per-frame cost does not scale with whatever the author drags in. The pre-scale happens once via canvas drawImage before the image reaches the filter graph and the chain contains no scale at all - the first draft's in-graph scale=3840:2160 measured as the slowest of four options (56.9s vs 51.8s) because -loop 1 pushes 300 frames and the filter re-scaled one static image three hundred times. Target is 2x canvas width, never upscaling past the source.

nodes.label: kenBurnsAt(move, t01) - one function of time
nodes.rationale: ADR-0008 and ADR-0010 both landed on one module with two emitters, and a per-Beat rotation once shipped with an inverted sign because preview and export were computed separately. It is not ticked per frame: it generates CSS keyframes for GPU-smooth playback and is sampled directly while paused or scrubbing, because a running CSS animation cannot be scrubbed and both the Still preview and the trimmer have scrubbers.

nodes.label: Linear interpolation, no easing field
nodes.rationale: For CSS keyframes and zoompan to agree the interpolation must be exactly expressible in both; linear is start + (end-start)*t on both sides while a cubic-bezier would need sampling into N stops and N piecewise segments, machinery hiding the fact that easing is imperceptible on a 1.2x drift over ten seconds. Adding the field later is close to free because an absent optional field means 'the old default' - as Clip.kind and the google: font id already demonstrated.

nodes.label: Ken Burns 1.0 means contain; Fill preset
nodes.rationale: Zoom 1x already means the frame untouched with letterbox bars, so if Ken Burns 1.0 meant 'fill the canvas' two scales would share a number and switching modes would silently reinterpret every value. The cost is a portrait Still starting mostly black, so a Fill preset computes that Still's exact cover scale - one click, but the author's decision rather than the tool silently cropping their photograph. The zoom ceiling is available pixels, not a fixed cap: a 3:4 photo needs ~2.37x merely to fill 16:9.

nodes.label: Ken Burns export cost (+27% time, ~14x bytes)
nodes.rationale: Export time for a Still Beat rises roughly a quarter, bounded not eliminated by the pre-scale. The exported file grows about 14x (1.1 MB -> 15.1 MB on a 10s Still) because a static Still's P-frames are empty while a moving one changes every macroblock; those bytes flow into the concat and final mux, so the cost is export-wide and independent of the pre-scale.

nodes.label: Move stored as start/end, never as a rate
nodes.rationale: Retrimming a Beat re-fits the same journey, faster - following the Sticker fitToBeat rule: derived at read time, never written back, so a retrim cannot leave a stale duration behind. Six values are stored even though v1 ships presets, keeping presets a UI affordance rather than a data model.

nodes.label: Layer (composited onto a Segment)
nodes.rationale: Four composited things - a Caption, a Title overlay, a B-roll Overlay and a Sticker - become adapters over one narrow interface { inputs, inputArgs, chains, inputCount }, assembled by a module owning input ordering, index assignment, label naming and which stage emits [v]. Layer is a glossary term because the author already manipulates four instances of it.

nodes.label: The picture itself is not a Layer
nodes.rationale: 'Everything is a Layer' was rejected because the base is a different kind of thing: Ken Burns replaces scale+pad (it is how the picture is produced), the intro Zoom forks the stream with split=2, and the Grade is a lut3d inside the base chain reading a sidecar that consumes no input index. The interface would need 'I am the source' and 'I fork the stream', concepts no other member uses. The boundary keeps paying: it settles without a special case that grade.cube needs no modelling as an input-that-is-not-an-input, because every Layer's file is indexed by definition.

nodes.label: Segment (seg_N.mp4 pipeline artifact)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not a glossary term - one Beat rendered to seg_N.mp4 before concat, which the author never encounters; defined in the module header instead.

nodes.label: Scattered index formulas and isLast sites
nodes.rationale: Four hand-derived index formulas (1+capCount+k, 1+capCount+titleCount+ovIdx, stickerIdxBase+k, stickerIdxBase+stickerCount), six isLast sites each encoding the population of every later stage, and one argv concatenation that is the only place the real input order exists. None fails at compile time; a missed edit gives an opaque wasm error or a graph that succeeds and composites the wrong bitmap.

nodes.label: SegmentTitleOverlay as-any triple cast
nodes.rationale: Declared { pngName: string; filter: string } but filter is stuffed with an object through as any at both push sites and read back with a third; the declared type is a lie in three places because the shape did not fit and was forced rather than widened honestly - the same failure a Layer interface stretched to cover the base would repeat.

nodes.label: rgbFormat as a parameter of the whole builder
nodes.rationale: So the retry produces two complete, internally consistent graphs. Today base/caption/title chains are built outside the retry while overlay/sticker are rebuilt inside it, freezing half the [v] decisions before the other half is made. Encoder flags, quality profile and the audio chain stay outside because both retry ladders (gbrp->null, source->silent) retry with different args over the same graph - the graph should not know retries exist.

nodes.label: Overlay Video Clips Library
nodes.rationale: Categorised overlay video clips (B-roll, film grain, light leaks, glitch, blend transitions) loaded and layered into video projects.

nodes.label: caption-font.ttf
nodes.rationale: Used for burned-in captions in the export, loaded same-origin then written into the ffmpeg filesystem to avoid CDN/CORS fragility. The exporter only needs a valid .ttf at /caption-font.ttf.

nodes.label: fonts/title-sans.ttf and fonts/title-serif.ttf
nodes.rationale: Arial Bold and Georgia Bold copies backing the Sans-serif / Serif title overlay choices. Users can also upload their own title font per export, which needs no bundled file.

nodes.label: Open-licence font replacement requirement
nodes.rationale: The bundled files are proprietary placeholders (Arial/Georgia) grabbed because the open-font download was network-blocked; they must be replaced with open-licensed TTFs (Roboto, Inter, DejaVu Sans/Serif, Lora; OFL/Apache) before distributing the app.

nodes.label: Spike: client-side 1080p export
nodes.rationale: Proves (or breaks) ADR-0002: each clip is trimmed, scaled and letterboxed to 1920x1080, optionally gets a burned-in caption, and all clips are concatenated into one MP4 entirely in the browser via ffmpeg.wasm, watching DevTools memory, total time and peak JS heap.

nodes.label: Ken Burns spike - is zoompan fast enough in wasm?
nodes.rationale: Throwaway measurement for ADR-0015 running a 10s Still Beat segment (300 frames @ 30fps, 1920x1080 out) four ways through the app's own runIsolated and self-hosted cores, single-threaded because MT_ENABLED is off by kill-switch in ffmpegEngine.ts - so the numbers are the real pipeline and what users get.

nodes.label: Pre-scale measurement result (2x was slowest)
nodes.rationale: Baseline 31.4s (3.14x realtime); in-graph pre-scale 1.5x 48.2s (+53%); in-graph pre-scale 2x 56.9s (+81%); no pre-scale raw 6000w 51.8s (+65%). The 2x pre-scale ADR-0015 originally specified was the slowest of four, worse than no pre-scale at all, because -loop 1 pushes 300 frames and scale re-scaled one static image three hundred times. The ADR was corrected to a single canvas drawImage (renderStillContained) before the bytes reach ffmpeg.

nodes.label: Outstanding: corrected approach projected, not measured
nodes.rationale: The ~40s (+27%) figure is projected: none of the four cases measures the one-time-pre-scale path that actually shipped. Re-run against the real implementation before trusting it. Also: a moving Beat is ~14x the bytes (1.1 -> 15.1 MB) independent of pre-scale, and the 31.4s baseline is 0.32x realtime, matching HYBRID_EXPORT_PLAN.md's ~0.3x figure.

nodes.label: Ken Burns spike harness page
nodes.rationale: Renders one 10s Still Beat segment four ways through the app's own engine and self-hosted cores to measure ADR-0015's pre-scale choice against the no-move baseline; the verdict text frames the 1.5x vs 2x gap as the jitter-vs-speed trade.

nodes.label: makeStill(w, h) synthetic 6000px photo
nodes.rationale: A gradient plus 6000 random 3px specks so scaler cost is realistic rather than trivially compressible.

nodes.label: kb(preW, preH, z0, z1) zoompan chain builder
nodes.rationale: Linear zoompan over the frame index - the exact shape ADR-0015 specifies: z='z0+(z1-z0)*on/(FRAMES-1)', x/y centred, d=1, s=1920x1080, fps=30.

nodes.label: runIsolated (ffmpegEngine)
nodes.rationale: The app's own isolated ffmpeg runner, used by the spike so the measurement is the real pipeline; multithreadReady() is logged alongside.

nodes.label: Spike: Claude clip descriptions
nodes.rationale: Tests ADR-0001: grabs a few frames per clip via <video> + <canvas> downscaled, sends them to a Claude vision model, and shows the returned Clip Description. The success test is whether descriptions are distinct and concrete enough that a downstream editor could sequence a story from them alone.

nodes.label: Vision model choice (haiku-4-5 / sonnet-5 / opus-4-8)
nodes.rationale: claude-haiku-4-5 is the cheap, likely per-clip default; sonnet-5 mid; opus-4-8 strongest and priciest.

nodes.label: Browser-held Anthropic API key trade-off
nodes.rationale: The key is pasted in memory and never stored, riding in the browser - the same knowingly-accepted trade-off as ADR-0002. Fine for a personal spike; a public app would proxy it.

nodes.label: stickers/ asset library
nodes.rationale: Drop .png, .svg or .webp files here and they appear in the Sticker picker; uploading through the picker writes into this folder too, so an uploaded sticker joins the library permanently.

nodes.label: /api/stickers dev endpoint (vite.config.ts)
nodes.rationale: Serves the folder in dev, mirroring the audio/ SFX library.
